claim: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 6 (SCA6) is characterized by cerebellar dysfunction.
source: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 6 (SCA6) is a rare disease that is characterized by cerebellar dysfunction.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract describing the disease characteristics.

claim: SCA6 patients have progressive motor coordination impairment.
source: Patients have progressive motor coordination impairment, and postmortem brain tissue reveals degeneration of cerebellar Purkinje cells and a reduced level of cerebellar brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF).
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of SCA6 patients.

claim: Postmortem brain tissue from SCA6 patients reveals degeneration of cerebellar Purkinje cells.
source: Patients have progressive motor coordination impairment, and postmortem brain tissue reveals degeneration of cerebellar Purkinje cells and a reduced level of cerebellar brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF).
evidence: This is stated as a known finding from postmortem tissue analysis.

claim: Postmortem brain tissue from SCA6 patients shows a reduced level of cerebellar BDNF.
source: Patients have progressive motor coordination impairment, and postmortem brain tissue reveals degeneration of cerebellar Purkinje cells and a reduced level of cerebellar brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF).
evidence: This is stated as a known finding from postmortem tissue analysis.

claim: RNA-sequencing of cerebellar vermis tissue in a mouse model of SCA6 revealed widespread dysregulation of genes associated with the endo-lysosomal system.
source: We carried out RNA-sequencing of cerebellar vermis tissue in a mouse model of SCA6, which revealed widespread dysregulation of genes associated with the endo-lysosomal system.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the RNA-sequencing results from the study.

claim: Early endosomes were enlarged in the Purkinje cells of SCA6 mice.
source: We identified alterations in multiple endosomal compartments in the Purkinje cells of SCA6 mice. Early endosomes were enlarged, while the size of the late endosome compartment was reduced.
evidence: This is a direct statement of findings from the study.

claim: The size of the late endosome compartment was reduced in the Purkinje cells of SCA6 mice.
source: We identified alterations in multiple endosomal compartments in the Purkinje cells of SCA6 mice. Early endosomes were enlarged, while the size of the late endosome compartment was reduced.
evidence: This is a direct statement of findings from the study.

claim: There is evidence for impaired trafficking of cargo to the lysosomes in SCA6 mice.
source: We also found evidence for impaired trafficking of cargo to the lysosomes.
evidence: This is a direct statement of findings from the study.

claim: The enlarged early endosomes in SCA6 mice accumulated both BDNF and TrkB.
source: Indeed, we found that the enlarged early endosomes in SCA6 mice accumulated both BDNF and TrkB.
evidence: This is a direct statement of findings from the study.

claim: TrkB recycling to the cell membrane in recycling endosomes was reduced in SCA6 mice.
source: Furthermore, TrkB recycling to the cell membrane in recycling endosomes was reduced, and the late endosome transport of BDNF for degradation was impaired.
evidence: This is a direct statement of findings from the study.

claim: Late endosome transport of BDNF for degradation was impaired in SCA6 mice.
source: Furthermore, TrkB recycling to the cell membrane in recycling endosomes was reduced, and the late endosome transport of BDNF for degradation was impaired.
evidence: This is a direct statement of findings from the study.

claim: Deficits in early endosomes and BDNF localization were rescued by chronic administration of 7,8-dihydroxyflavone (7,8-DHF).
source: Deficits in early endosomes and BDNF localization were rescued by chronic administration of a TrkB agonist, 7,8-dihydroxyflavone, that we have previously shown restores motor coordination and cerebellar TrkB expression.
evidence: This is a direct statement of findings from the study.

claim: 7,8-DHF has previously been shown to restore motor coordination in SCA6 mice.
source: Deficits in early endosomes and BDNF localization were rescued by chronic administration of a TrkB agonist, 7,8-dihydroxyflavone, that we have previously shown restores motor coordination and cerebellar TrkB expression.
evidence: This references previous work by the authors.

claim: 7,8-DHF has previously been shown to restore cerebellar TrkB expression in SCA6 mice.
source: Deficits in early endosomes and BDNF localization were rescued by chronic administration of a TrkB agonist, 7,8-dihydroxyflavone, that we have previously shown restores motor coordination and cerebellar TrkB expression.
evidence: This references previous work by the authors.

claim: SCA6 is caused by a CAG expansion mutation that generates an expanded polyglutamine tract in the translated protein.
source: It is caused by a CAG expansion mutation that generates an expanded polyglutamine tract in the translated protein (Zhuchenko et al., 1997).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: The affected gene in SCA6 is CACNA1A.
source: The affected gene is CACNA1A (Zhuchenko et al., 1997), which encodes both the alpha subunit of voltage-gated calcium P/Q channels and a putative transcription factor (Du et al., 2019; Du et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: CACNA1A encodes the alpha subunit of voltage-gated calcium P/Q channels.
source: The affected gene is CACNA1A (Zhuchenko et al., 1997), which encodes both the alpha subunit of voltage-gated calcium P/Q channels and a putative transcription factor (Du et al., 2019; Du et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: CACNA1A encodes a putative transcription factor.
source: The affected gene is CACNA1A (Zhuchenko et al., 1997), which encodes both the alpha subunit of voltage-gated calcium P/Q channels and a putative transcription factor (Du et al., 2019; Du et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: The endo-lysosomal system comprises a series of membrane-bound compartments that sort and transport endocytosed molecules destined for recycling or degradation.
source: The endo-lysosomal system comprises of a series of membrane-bound compartments that sort and transport endocytosed molecules destined for recycling or degradation (Figure 1a; Hu et al., 2015; Huotari and Helenius, 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations and reference to a figure.

claim: Each compartment of the endo-lysosomal system has a characteristic pH mediated by ATP-dependent acidification.
source: Each compartment has a characteristic pH mediated by ATP-dependent acidification (Hu et al., 2015), and is characterized by the presence of specific proteins that allow them to carry out their functions.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Rab GTPases regulate trafficking of cargo in the endo-lysosomal system.
source: Rab GTPases regulate trafficking of cargo, and each compartment is associated with a specific signature of Rab family members (Stenmark, 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Each compartment of the endo-lysosomal system is associated with a specific signature of Rab family members.
source: Rab GTPases regulate trafficking of cargo, and each compartment is associated with a specific signature of Rab family members (Stenmark, 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Endocytosed cargo arrives first at the early endosomes.
source: Endocytosed cargo arrives first at the early endosomes (Ludwig et al., 1991), where the slightly acidic pH leads to dissociation of ligands from their receptors.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: The slightly acidic pH in early endosomes leads to dissociation of ligands from their receptors.
source: Endocytosed cargo arrives first at the early endosomes (Ludwig et al., 1991), where the slightly acidic pH leads to dissociation of ligands from their receptors.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Late endosomes are characterized by an increasingly acidic pH and increased enzymatic activity.
source: Cargo that is destined for further sorting or degradation will move to the late endosomes, which are characterized by an increasingly acidic pH and increased enzymatic activity (Hu et al., 2015; Huotari and Helenius, 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: The lysosome is the final destination of cargo that is to be degraded.
source: The lysosome is the final destination of cargo that is to be degraded.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: The lysosome is the most acidic compartment of the endo-lysosomal system.
source: This compartment is the most acidic and contains over 50 hydrolases that carry out rapid degradation of cargo (de Duve, 2005; Lawrence and Zoncu, 2019).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: The lysosome contains over 50 hydrolases that carry out rapid degradation of cargo.
source: This compartment is the most acidic and contains over 50 hydrolases that carry out rapid degradation of cargo (de Duve, 2005; Lawrence and Zoncu, 2019).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Postmortem brain tissue from Alzheimer's disease patients displays increased early endosome size.
source: A notable example is Alzheimer's disease, where postmortem brain tissue from patients displays increased early endosome size and accumulation of cargo (Cataldo et al., 2004; Cataldo et al., 2000; Cataldo et al., 1997; Tate and Mathews, 2006).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Postmortem brain tissue from Alzheimer's disease patients displays accumulation of cargo in early endosomes.
source: A notable example is Alzheimer's disease, where postmortem brain tissue from patients displays increased early endosome size and accumulation of cargo (Cataldo et al., 2004; Cataldo et al., 2000; Cataldo et al., 1997; Tate and Mathews, 2006).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Similar early endosome changes are seen in Down syndrome.
source: Similar early endosome changes are seen in Down syndrome (Cataldo et al., 2000) and Niemann Pick C (Jin et al., 2004; Kim et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Similar early endosome changes are seen in Niemann Pick C.
source: Similar early endosome changes are seen in Down syndrome (Cataldo et al., 2000) and Niemann Pick C (Jin et al., 2004; Kim et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Endo-lysosomal dysfunction in the cerebellum can lead to cerebellar dysfunction.
source: In the cerebellum, endo-lysosomal dysfunction can lead to cerebellar dysfunction (Akizu et al., 2015; Mannan et al., 2004; Sterling et al., 2023; Vanier, 2010), and has been identified in cerebellar diseases with diverse disease-causing mechanisms (Alves et al., 2014; Zhu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Endo-lysosomal dysfunction has been identified in cerebellar diseases with diverse disease-causing mechanisms.
source: In the cerebellum, endo-lysosomal dysfunction can lead to cerebellar dysfunction (Akizu et al., 2015; Mannan et al., 2004; Sterling et al., 2023; Vanier, 2010), and has been identified in cerebellar diseases with diverse disease-causing mechanisms (Alves et al., 2014; Zhu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Lysosomal accumulation of protein aggregates has been observed in a mouse model of SCA6 (118Q) that features a hyperexpanded polyglutamine repeat.
source: Previously, lysosomal accumulation of protein aggregates has been observed in a mouse model of SCA6 (118Q) that features a hyperexpanded polyglutamine repeat (Unno et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Cerebellar pathology in the SCA6 118Q mouse model was worsened when lysosomal function was impaired by the loss of the lysosomal enzyme cathepsin B.
source: Cerebellar pathology in this model was worsened when lysosomal function was impaired by the loss of the lysosomal enzyme cathepsin B (Unno et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Deficits in the BDNF–TrkB–Akt signaling pathway contribute to SCA6 pathophysiology.
source: We have recently found that deficits in the brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)–tropomyosin kinase B (TrkB)–Akt signaling pathway contribute to SCA6 pathophysiology (Cook et al., 2022), with both BDNF and TrkB expression reduced in the cerebellar vermis.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous work by the authors with a citation.

claim: Both BDNF and TrkB expression are reduced in the cerebellar vermis in SCA6.
source: We have recently found that deficits in the brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)–tropomyosin kinase B (TrkB)–Akt signaling pathway contribute to SCA6 pathophysiology (Cook et al., 2022), with both BDNF and TrkB expression reduced in the cerebellar vermis.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous work by the authors with a citation.

claim: BDNF and TrkB are dynamically trafficked through the endo-lysosomal system.
source: Since both BDNF and TrkB are dynamically trafficked through the endo-lysosomal system (Moya-Alvarado et al., 2023; Moya-Alvarado et al., 2018; Yamashita and Kuruvilla, 2016), we wondered whether dysfunction in this system could underlie BDNF and/or TrkB mislocalization, contributing to subsequent cellular dysfunction in SCA6.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: SCA684Q/84Q mice robustly model the mid-life onset of motor deficits and cerebellar dysfunction seen in SCA6 patients.
source: Here, we address whether endo-lysosomal dysfunction contributes to SCA6, using a mouse model (SCA684Q/84Q mice, referred to as SCA6 mice) that robustly models the mid-life onset of motor deficits and cerebellar dysfunction seen in SCA6 patients (Jayabal et al., 2015; Watase et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Around 7 months of age, SCA6 mice develop deficits in motor coordination that progressively worsen.
source: We have previously shown that around 7 months of age, SCA6 mice develop deficits in motor coordination that progressively worsen (Jayabal et al., 2015; Jayabal et al., 2016) and display cellular deficits, including aberrant Purkinje cell firing and disrupted BDNF–TrkB signaling (Cook et al., 2022; Chang et al., 2022; Jayabal et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous work by the authors with citations.

claim: SCA6 mice display aberrant Purkinje cell firing.
source: We have previously shown that around 7 months of age, SCA6 mice develop deficits in motor coordination that progressively worsen (Jayabal et al., 2015; Jayabal et al., 2016) and display cellular deficits, including aberrant Purkinje cell firing and disrupted BDNF–TrkB signaling (Cook et al., 2022; Chang et al., 2022; Jayabal et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous work by the authors with citations.

claim: SCA6 mice display disrupted BDNF–TrkB signaling.
source: We have previously shown that around 7 months of age, SCA6 mice develop deficits in motor coordination that progressively worsen (Jayabal et al., 2015; Jayabal et al., 2016) and display cellular deficits, including aberrant Purkinje cell firing and disrupted BDNF–TrkB signaling (Cook et al., 2022; Chang et al., 2022; Jayabal et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous work by the authors with citations.

claim: Many genes involved in the endo-lysosomal system were significantly dysregulated in the SCA6 cerebellum.
source: This sequencing revealed that many genes involved in the endo-lysosomal system, as defined by the gene ontology (GO:CC) terms 'Endosome' (GO:0005768) and 'Lysosome' (GO:0005764), were significantly dysregulated in the SCA6 cerebellum (Figure 1b, padj < 0.05, see Table 1 for a full list).
evidence: This is a direct statement of RNA-sequencing results with reference to a figure and table.

claim: The expression levels of endo-lysosomal genes were altered by between 10% and 200% in SCA6 compared to WT.
source: The expression levels of these genes were altered by between 10% and 200% in SCA6 compared to WT.
evidence: This is a direct statement of RNA-sequencing results.

claim: Endosomal genes were found to be both up- and downregulated in SCA6.
source: Endosomal genes were found to be both up- and downregulated in SCA6, but the genes covered by the Lysosome GO term were mostly upregulated compared to WT.
evidence: This is a direct statement of RNA-sequencing results.

claim: The genes covered by the Lysosome GO term were mostly upregulated in SCA6 compared to WT.
source: Endosomal genes were found to be both up- and downregulated in SCA6, but the genes covered by the Lysosome GO term were mostly upregulated compared to WT.
evidence: This is a direct statement of RNA-sequencing results.

claim: EEA1 staining is present in the cerebellum, particularly in Purkinje cells.
source: We carried out immunohistochemistry (IHC) against early endosome antigen 1 (EEA1) on sections of cerebellar vermis from 7- to 8-month WT and SCA6 mice and found that EEA1 staining is present in the cerebellum, particularly in Purkinje cells (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to a figure.

claim: Large tubular early endosomes can be identified in Purkinje cell somas of both WT and SCA6 mice.
source: We imaged Purkinje cells and could identify large tubular early endosomes in Purkinje cell somas of both WT and SCA6 mice (Figure 2b, c).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to figures.

claim: The early endosome marker in SCA6 Purkinje cells covered a larger area, showing that the early endosome compartment is enlarged in SCA6.
source: The early endosome marker in SCA6 Purkinje cells covered a larger area, showing that the early endosome compartment is enlarged in SCA6 (Figure 2c,d).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to figures.

claim: There was a higher amount of BDNF staining within the early endosomes of Purkinje cells from SCA6 mice.
source: There was a higher amount of BDNF staining within the early endosomes of Purkinje cells from SCA6 mice (Figure 2e, f).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to figures.

claim: BDNF levels in the cerebellar vermis as a whole are decreased in SCA6.
source: This was intriguing as we have previously shown that BDNF levels in the cerebellar vermis as a whole are decreased (Cook et al., 2022), so BDNF accumulates specifically in this compartment despite depressed levels overall in the cerebellum.
evidence: This references previous work by the authors with a citation.

claim: TrkB immunoreactivity was increased within the EEA1-positive early endosome compartment in SCA6 Purkinje cells compared to WT.
source: We found the same was true for TrkB, as TrkB immunoreactivity was increased within the EEA1-positive early endosome compartment in SCA6 Purkinje cells compared to WT (Figure 2g, h).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to figures.

claim: Nearly all of the TrkB staining within SCA6 Purkinje cells colocalized with the EEA1 marker.
source: Nearly all of the TrkB staining within SCA6 Purkinje cells colocalized with the EEA1 marker (Figure 2g, arrowheads), whereas the tissue from WT mice showed abundant TrkB staining outside the early endosome compartment of Purkinje cells (Figure 2g, arrowheads).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to a figure.

claim: Tissue from WT mice showed abundant TrkB staining outside the early endosome compartment of Purkinje cells.
source: Nearly all of the TrkB staining within SCA6 Purkinje cells colocalized with the EEA1 marker (Figure 2g, arrowheads), whereas the tissue from WT mice showed abundant TrkB staining outside the early endosome compartment of Purkinje cells (Figure 2g, arrowheads).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to a figure.

claim: Cargo mis-trafficking could lead to a decrease in the amount of free BDNF available to signal in SCA6.
source: Thus, early endosomes are enlarged and accumulate BDNF and TrkB in SCA6, despite decreased levels of both proteins in the SCA6 cerebellum as a whole. This cargo mis-trafficking could lead to a decrease in the amount of free BDNF available to signal, as well as the amount of TrkB recycled to the cell surface, thereby contributing to previously described BDNF–TrkB signaling deficits in SCA6 (Cook et al., 2022).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings and previous work.

claim: Cargo mis-trafficking could lead to a decrease in the amount of TrkB recycled to the cell surface in SCA6.
source: Thus, early endosomes are enlarged and accumulate BDNF and TrkB in SCA6, despite decreased levels of both proteins in the SCA6 cerebellum as a whole. This cargo mis-trafficking could lead to a decrease in the amount of free BDNF available to signal, as well as the amount of TrkB recycled to the cell surface, thereby contributing to previously described BDNF–TrkB signaling deficits in SCA6 (Cook et al., 2022).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings and previous work.

claim: Syntaxin 12/13 (Stx13) is involved in recycling of endocytosed proteins back to the plasma membrane.
source: Syntaxin 12/13 (Stx13) is involved in recycling of endocytosed proteins back to the plasma membrane and is located in recycling endosomes and some tubular protrusions from early endosomes that are also involved in recycling (Prekeris et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Stx13 is located in recycling endosomes and some tubular protrusions from early endosomes that are also involved in recycling.
source: Syntaxin 12/13 (Stx13) is involved in recycling of endocytosed proteins back to the plasma membrane and is located in recycling endosomes and some tubular protrusions from early endosomes that are also involved in recycling (Prekeris et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Staining with two different Stx13 antibodies revealed a large network of small recycling endosomes and protrusions in Purkinje cells.
source: Staining with both antibodies revealed a large network of small recycling endosomes and protrusions in Purkinje cells (Figure 3b, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to figures.

claim: Recycling endosome area was unchanged in SCA6 Purkinje cells.
source: Analysis of the staining with both antibodies showed that recycling endosome area was unchanged in SCA6 Purkinje cells (Figure 3c, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to figures.

claim: There is colocalization between TrkB and Stx13, showing TrkB being recycled back to the cell surface after dissociation from bound BDNF in the early endosomes.
source: We noted colocalization between TrkB and Stx13, showing TrkB being recycled back to the cell surface after dissociation from bound BDNF in the early endosomes.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings.

claim: The TrkB staining within the recycling endosome compartment marked by Stx13 was decreased in Purkinje cells in SCA6 mice.
source: The TrkB staining within the recycling endosome compartment marked by Stx13 was decreased in Purkinje cells in SCA6 mice (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to a figure.

claim: TrkB is stuck in early endosomes in SCA6, rather than being recycled to the cell surface to the same extent as in WT Purkinje cells.
source: Combined with the increased levels of TrkB in the early endosomes of Purkinje cells in SCA6 (Figure 2h), these data argue that TrkB is stuck in early endosomes in SCA6, rather than being recycled to the cell surface to the same extent as in WT Purkinje cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings.

claim: TrkB mislocalization may contribute to the depressed levels of BDNF–TrkB signaling previously described in SCA6.
source: This mislocalization may contribute to the depressed levels of BDNF–TrkB signaling previously described in SCA6 (Cook et al., 2022).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings and previous work.

claim: Early endosomes undergo maturation into late endosomes in order to transport cargo destined for degradation to the lysosomes.
source: Early endosomes undergo maturation into late endosomes in order to transport cargo destined for degradation to the lysosomes (Huotari and Helenius, 2011; Figure 4a).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation and reference to a figure.

claim: Neurons use the degradative pathway as a way to regulate BDNF levels.
source: Neurons use this degradative pathway as a way to regulate BDNF levels (Evans et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Rab7 is a marker for late endosomes.
source: We used Rab7 as a marker for late endosomes (Vitelli et al., 1997), and identified numerous late endosomes in Purkinje cells of both WT and SCA6 mice (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation and reference to experimental findings.

claim: Numerous late endosomes were identified in Purkinje cells of both WT and SCA6 mice.
source: We used Rab7 as a marker for late endosomes (Vitelli et al., 1997), and identified numerous late endosomes in Purkinje cells of both WT and SCA6 mice (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to a figure.

claim: The Rab7 staining covered a smaller area in the Purkinje cells of SCA6 mice compared to WT.
source: The Rab7 staining covered a smaller area in the Purkinje cells of SCA6 mice compared to WT (Figure 4c), indicating a reduction in the size or number of late endosomes.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to a figure.

claim: Most of the BDNF staining within the Purkinje cells did not colocalize with Rab7.
source: Most of the BDNF staining within the Purkinje cells did not colocalize with Rab7 (Figure 4b), which was expected as we had previously found high levels of colocalization of BDNF with the early endosome marker EEA1 (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to figures.

claim: The BDNF staining that was present within the Rab7-positive late endosome compartment was significantly reduced in SCA6 compared to WT.
source: The BDNF staining that was present within the Rab7-positive late endosome compartment was significantly reduced in SCA6 compared to WT (Figure 4d), suggesting that BDNF accumulates in the early endosomes earlier in the endosomal pathway (Figure 2f), preventing its progression through the late endosomal stage.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to figures.

claim: BDNF accumulates in the early endosomes earlier in the endosomal pathway, preventing its progression through the late endosomal stage in SCA6.
source: The BDNF staining that was present within the Rab7-positive late endosome compartment was significantly reduced in SCA6 compared to WT (Figure 4d), suggesting that BDNF accumulates in the early endosomes earlier in the endosomal pathway (Figure 2f), preventing its progression through the late endosomal stage.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings.

claim: Less BDNF may reach the lysosome in SCA6.
source: Late endosomes transport cargo to lysosomes for degradation, so less BDNF may reach the lysosome in SCA6.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings.

claim: The proper functioning of the endo-lysosomal system is crucial for the sorting and trafficking of signaling molecules.
source: As the proper functioning of the endo-lysosomal system is crucial for the sorting and trafficking of signaling molecules, we wondered whether these changes could contribute to previously identified deficits in signaling by BDNF and its receptor tropomyosin kinase B (TrkB) in SCA6.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: LysoTracker Red DND 99 is a pH-sensitive dye that visualizes acidic lysosomes.
source: We first used a pH-sensitive dye, LysoTracker Red DND 99, to visualize the acidic lysosomes (Figure 5a, b; Chazotte, 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation and reference to figures.

claim: LysoTracker labels all acidic compartments.
source: As LysoTracker labels all acidic compartments, it is not sufficient to confirm the identity of lysosomes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Lamp1 is a glycoprotein localized at the membranes of lysosomes.
source: Therefore, after staining acute cerebellar slices with LysoTracker, we performed IHC for Lysosomal-associated membrane protein 1 (Lamp1), a glycoprotein localized at the membranes of lysosomes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Both LysoTracker and Lamp1 stains labelled lysosomes within Purkinje cells.
source: We found that both stains labelled lysosomes within Purkinje cells (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to a figure.

claim: The Lamp1 staining appeared as ring-like structures, marking the membranes of the lysosomes.
source: As expected, the Lamp1 staining appeared as ring-like structures, marking the membranes of the lysosomes, while LysoTracker staining marked the acidic lumen of the lysosomes, in the center of these rings (Figure 5b, see zoom).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to a figure.

claim: LysoTracker staining marked the acidic lumen of the lysosomes, in the center of the Lamp1-positive rings.
source: As expected, the Lamp1 staining appeared as ring-like structures, marking the membranes of the lysosomes, while LysoTracker staining marked the acidic lumen of the lysosomes, in the center of these rings (Figure 5b, see zoom).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to a figure.

claim: Lamp1 staining identified a large number of lysosomes of varying size, while the LysoTracker stain was present only in the largest.
source: While Lamp1 staining identified a large number of lysosomes of varying size, the LysoTracker stain was present only in the largest.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings.

claim: LysoTracker does not label the smallest lysosomes in cerebellar slices or other cell preparations that are fixed after staining.
source: This discrepancy has been noted previously, as LysoTracker does not label the smallest lysosomes in cerebellar slices or other cell preparations that are fixed after staining (Chazotte, 2011; Song et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: The total area covered by the Lamp1 stain was not significantly different between Purkinje cells from WT and SCA6 mice.
source: We found that the total area covered by the Lamp1 and LysoTracker stains was not significantly different between Purkinje cells from WT and SCA6 mice (Figure 5c, d).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to figures.

claim: The total area covered by the LysoTracker stain was not significantly different between Purkinje cells from WT and SCA6 mice.
source: We found that the total area covered by the Lamp1 and LysoTracker stains was not significantly different between Purkinje cells from WT and SCA6 mice (Figure 5c, d).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to figures.

claim: The area of colocalization between Lamp1 and LysoTracker was unchanged between WT and SCA6 mice.
source: The area of colocalization between the two stains was also unchanged (Figure 5e).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to a figure.

claim: The number of lysosomes labeled by both Lamp1 and LysoTracker was indistinguishable between WT and SCA6 mice.
source: The number of these lysosomes was indistinguishable between WT and SCA6 mice (Figure 5f), indicating that Lamp1-positive lysosomes are present in normal quantities and are appropriately acidified in SCA6 Purkinje cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings with reference to a figure.

claim: Lamp1-positive lysosomes are present in normal quantities and are appropriately acidified in SCA6 Purkinje cells.
source: The number of these lysosomes was indistinguishable between WT and SCA6 mice (Figure 5f), indicating that Lamp1-positive lysosomes are present in normal quantities and are appropriately acidified in SCA6 Purkinje cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings.

claim: The number of lysosomes labeled by Lamp1 but not LysoTracker was not significantly different between WT and SCA6 mice.
source: This number was not significantly different between WT and SCA6 mice and so Lamp1 appears to be present at normal levels and is appropriately localized to lysosomes in SCA6.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings.

claim: Lamp1 appears to be present at normal levels and is appropriately localized to lysosomes in SCA6.
source: This number was not significantly different between WT and SCA6 mice and so Lamp1 appears to be present at normal levels and is appropriately localized to lysosomes in SCA6.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings.

claim: The number of organelles labeled by LysoTracker but not Lamp1 was significantly lower in SCA6 mice.
